scope: New publication Git policy and its real-Git fixture tests; no global documentation claim.

contracts.docstring: A ref transaction may have committed; prove original process closure and inspect its marker before any further effect.
Trusted port whose original broker manifest must bind the complete immutable transaction input and its fresh authority.
Original Git metadata identity that must be persisted by admission and pinned by the physical executor.
Original registration, exact captured candidate and pinned metadata; this data is not acceptance or effect authority.
An original host publication identity and explicitly observed branch; absent is distinct from an unknown destination.
Historical effect evidence with destination currentness separated from whether this request actually published.
Reject redirected/shared metadata before a publication port can expose source Git state in writing.
Bound all reads and the one explicit transaction to a single finite policy deadline and trusted executor.
Keep an applied request historical if another actor subsequently moves its branch.
Observe original atomic effect history only after independently proven original closure; never issue a replacement transaction.
Publish one exact candidate to a non-checked-out observed branch with one atomic branch/marker CAS; caller owns durable intent and fresh effect authority.
Write bounded fixed Git transaction input, collect complete output and prove original physical execution closure.
Capture an actual ordinary directory without adopting a symlink or a redirected path.
Require full same-format Git identities, complete evidence hashes and metadata belonging to these exact views before any command construction.
Forbid ambiguous refs and transaction injection before constructing any Git arguments.
Bind the marker namespace to the complete original destination observation as well as its host operation identity.
Retain the fresh host port without acquiring authority or changing its original lifetime.
Require complete bounded output and actual closure; a transport failure is never an empty successful read.
Read an exact full ref, ignoring longer prefix matches instead of adopting a similarly named branch.
Test-only real Git port; production must supply its freshly owned broker instead of this subprocess adapter.
Capture an actual accepted-version-shaped fixture with independent source and clean candidate checkout; no acceptance authority is simulated.
A ref command cannot smuggle another transaction, namespace or implicit destination.
Only the accepted candidate head and stable marker enter the source; its checked-out branch/files remain at the original base.
A physically closed original transaction is recovered by its atomic marker, even after the branch subsequently moves.
Publishing cannot update a checked-out branch or silently replace a different observed destination.
A matching commit name does not excuse modified captured source.
Losing observation after successful Git mutation must retain effect uncertainty just like a lost transaction response.
Another checkout also forbids a local branch ref update, even when the primary source has another branch open.
Actual ref CAS fails atomically if another writer creates the branch after preflight; no partial publication marker appears.
A copied Git directory with identical refs has a different origin; it cannot impersonate the original effect receipt.
Reusing a request label with a different destination is not evidence that the changed request published.
Stored Git expressions and abbreviated names cannot enter fixed Git invocations as candidate identities.
Retain actual transaction count and optional post-commit transport loss.
Use fixture paths directly; no claim of a production mount or effect grant.
Collect complete real local Git output within the policy deadline.
Execute the actual ref transaction once and optionally lose its completed response.
Own and drain this fixture process; uncertain test shutdown still kills and joins it.
Interrupt post-commit reads once while preserving the actual committed transaction.
Create the actual conflicting ref immediately before Git processes the original transaction.
